Chapline, children and heirs at law of Samuel H. Chapline, deceased'; the Moses W. Chapline heirs; defendants in Marshall, WETZEL and TYLER counties. person: George W. Caton & Mildred (Buckley); Wm P. Caton & Artemisia (Buckley) - Fairfax Co. VA heirs, non-resident 1851 = the Muskingum Catons
fact: THE MUSKINGUM CATONS CAME FROM FAIRFAX COUNTY, VIRGINIA - PROVED BY A CHANCERY CAUSE, AND IT PULLS MOSES B. CATON (1767-1839) INTO THE PRINCE WILLIAM-FAIRFAX BELT. Library of Virginia, Fairfax Co. chancery 1851-009, JOHN H. BUCKLEY v. MARGARET BUCKLEY, ANANIAS BUCKLEY, GEORGE W. CATON [Cayton], MILDRED CATON, Elizabeth & Jane Sinclair (53 images; cover, bill, summons, return and decree retained as evidence/Fairfax_1851-009_LVA_Buckley_v_Buckley_Caton_selected.zip). BILL (filed 1851): John Buckley the elder died seized of c.50 acres on CASTLE BRANCH, Fairfax Co. (tract from William Payne to John Fryer Buckley, 155 acres, Feb 1782, Lib. N f.525), leaving THIRTEEN children: James; Dora m. Thomas Sinclair; Sophia m. WM B. SEARS; Zephaniah; Susan m. Aquilla Croson; Charlotte; ARTEMISIA m. WM P. CAYTON; MILDRED m. GEO. W. CAYTON; Harriet m. Hezekiah Crouch; Jane m. Wm Marshall; Margaret; Ananias; John H. SUMMONS 15 Jul 1851 to the sheriff of Fairfax for 'Geo. W. Caton and Mildred his wife formerly Buckley' etc.; RETURN 21 Jul 1851: 'Affidavit of Jno. H. Buckley as to NON-RESIDENCE of all the defendants except Margaret Buckley' - George W. and Mildred Caton were living outside Virginia in 1851. DECREE: sale; $6.01 each to Margaret, Ananias and 'George W. Cayton who intermarried with Mildred Buckley'. IDENTIFICATION: this is George Wesley Caton (1805-53) of Roseville, Muskingum Co., Ohio, whose wife was Mildred (Buckley), 'natives of Virginia' (Goodspeed 1892; daughter Mildred b. Muskingum 1841 - C162), son of MOSES B. CATON b. 1767 Virginia, d. Muskingum 1839; and his brother William (George/P.) Caton married Artemisia Buckley, Mildred's sister; their sister Harriet Ann Caton married a SEARS - the Sears family that married Sophia Buckley. CONSEQUENCES. (1) Moses B. Caton's family lived in FAIRFAX CO. - two sons married daughters of John Buckley of Castle Branch c.1825-35 - before going to Muskingum in the 1830s. Fairfax adjoins Prince William; Castle Branch is in the Bull Run/Centreville country, a few miles from Broad Run. (2) The Prince William/Fauquier Moses (b. by 1781; Fauquier 1800-06; absent from Fauquier and Prince William after 1806 - C154, C156) and Moses B. of Muskingum (b. 1767 Virginia) are now the same man in all probability: same forename, right age, adjoining county, and a family that left Virginia for Ohio in the 1830s - the same decade the Fauquier William-Ann-Laury cluster left for Ohio (C098). C162 RISES TO B. (3) STORY A THEREFORE HAD AN OHIO BRANCH BY THE 1830s (Muskingum, 60 miles from Delaware Co.) headed by Aaron's uncle Moses and cousins George Wesley and William - the first documented reason for a Fauquier Caton boy to be in central Ohio in 1841. (4) Other Fairfax causes with Caton among the surnames - 1829-001 Lewis v. Vallandingham (100 images) and 1836-004 Cornwell v. Moore (38 images; Buckley, Croson, Rector) - may hold Moses or his sons as deponents or debtors in Fairfax 1829-36; unread. TEST: Fairfax personal property tax lists 1807-1838 for Moses/George W./William Caton (Full-Text 'Caton', Fairfax, 1800-1840). Grade B.
place: Fairfax Co., Virginia / Muskingum Co., Ohio

person: William G. Caton - deponent, Fairfax Co., 1 Sep 1835 (Centreville)
fact: THE FAIRFAX CATONS WERE STILL IN FAIRFAX, AT CENTREVILLE, IN SEPTEMBER 1835 - which dates their move to Ohio to 1835-39, the same window as the Fauquier cluster's. Library of Virginia, Fairfax chancery 1836-004, Kitty Cornwell v. Archibald Moore (a horse-swap dispute over a mare with glanders; 38 images; cover, notice and deposition pages retained as evidence/Fairfax_1836-004_LVA_Cornwell_v_Moore_WmGCaton_deposition.zip). Depositions taken 1 Sept 1835 at the house of Fountain Holmes before James L. Triplett J.P.: Alexander S. Grigsby, Anthony McCready, Bailey Padgett, Enoch Grigsby, William T. Allen, and 'The deposition of WILLIAM G. CATON, taken at the same time & place & for the same purpose in presence of the parties, being first duly sworn deposeth & saith, that he was at CENTREVILLE where he saw the horse Kitty Cornwell had swapt with A. Moore for, & having heard a great talk among the neighbours about this horse being diseased with glanders, he was induced to examine him strictly & also see Mr. Enoch Grigsby & Mr. Crosen do the same ... [he] could discover no symptoms of any disease ...' signed 'Wm G. Caton'. READINGS: (1) William G. Caton (b. 1800-10; Fairfax 1830 household C166; m. Artemisia Buckley C164) was a Centreville-neighbourhood man in 1835 - western Fairfax on the Prince William line, a few miles from Broad Run and the Buckleys' Castle Branch. (2) With Moses's 1830 household (C166) and the family's non-residence by 1851 (C164) and Moses's death at Roseville in 1839 (C162), the Fairfax Catons left Virginia BETWEEN SEPT 1835 AND 1839 - the same years the Fauquier William-Ann-Laury cluster went to Ohio (c.1835, C098). Two branches of one family leaving for Ohio together is one migration, not two. (3) Nothing on Aaron. Grade A for the deposition; B for the migration reading.

person: Nancy Jane (Johnson) Caton Blevins, 1849-1936 - Aaron F. Caton's wife 1869-86; REVERSES C151
fact: THE 1869 NANCY JOHNSON MARRIAGE IS AARON F.'S AFTER ALL, AND SHE STAYED HIS WIFE UNTIL HE DIED - SO THE 1871 DIVORCE IS THEIRS TOO, FOLLOWED BY RECONCILIATION. Sedalia Democrat, 28 Jun 1936 (archive.org OCR, excerpt retained): 'Mrs. Nancy Jane Blevins, who died in Kansas City, June 17 ... was born in Morgan county, August 3, 1849. She was married to AARON CATON in 1869. To this union eight children were born, Georgia Woolery, now deceased, Will Caton, Gillie Caton, Alice Orr, Ada Johnson, Ida Mann and Bessie Smashey, all of Kansas City, Kas., and Eva Brown of Los Angeles. She also mothered three children of Aaron Caton by a former marriage, HENRY CATON, Marshall, MRS. BASLEE, Green Ridge, and LIZZIE MOON, now deceased ... Her husband, Aaron Caton, was killed in a train accident at Otterville in 1885 [1886, C052]. She was a widow 23 years, then married Charles Blevins who died in 1920.' Sedalia Democrat, 4 and 6 May 1956: 'Mrs. Virginia "Jennie" Baslee, 85 ... born in Cooper County Feb. 10, 1871, the daughter of the late Mr. and Mrs. Aaron Caton ... married in Cooper County Dec. 25, 18[89], to William Baslee ... two brothers, Will Caton and Gilbert [Gillie] Caton; three sisters, Mrs. Ada Johnson, Mrs. Eva Orr and Mrs. Ida Huff.' READINGS. (1) Nancy Jane Johnson (b. 1849) married Aaron F. Caton in 1869 = the 12 Oct 1869 licence (C053), bore him the eight children of the 1880 Otterville household (C052), raised his three by the O'Neal first wife (Henry, Elizabeth 'Lizzie', Virginia - the 1875 minors, C150), and was widowed by the 1886 rail accident. (2) THEREFORE THE 1871 DIVORCE (C151: 'married 12 Oct 1869, deserted 8 Apr 1870, divorced 19 Oct 1871') IS ALSO AARON F.'S - the same marriage date - and the couple RESUMED after the decree (Jennie b. Feb 1871 was conceived during the supposed desertion; seven more children followed). C151's reassignment of the marriage and divorce to the direct-line Aaron is WITHDRAWN; C053 returns to its 12 Sep position: probably Aaron F.'s. (3) The direct-line Aaron's June 1870 'no wife present' (C041) is again unexplained, and NO remarriage of his is known; T03's bracket for Sarah returns to 1860-78. (4) The obituaries' 'Mrs. Baslee' as a stepchild born Feb 1871 is a garble - she is Nancy's own. Grade A for the obituaries; the divorce-reconciliation reading B.
source: Sedalia Democrat 28 Jun 1936; 4 and 6 May 1956 (archive.org OCR, via full-text search 14 Sep 2026)

BOARD OF OVERSEERS OF THE POOR MINUTES, 1804-1845 - ONE VOLUME, Local Government Records Collection, Fauquier County Court Records, Library of Virginia; barcode 1125621, FAUQUIER COUNTY REEL 116, filmed by Backstage Library Works under LVA's Circuit Court Records Preservation Program. The minutes give 'the names of people receiving financial support, food, and clothing, as well as BINDING CHILDREN AS APPRENTICES, and the burial of the deceased.' Covers 1828-1836 exactly. (2) Virginia Auditor of Public Accounts, OVERSEER OF THE POOR ANNUAL REPORTS AND CHECKLISTS (APA 739) - independent state-level series, Fauquier holdings 1829-1851. (3) Fauquier County MINUTE BOOKS survive from 1759 (microfilm and index books, Virginiana Room, Warrenton Library); Fauquier is NOT a lost-records county. WHAT THE RECORD YIELDS: under County Court supervision the Overseers indentured children to masters to learn a trade; the entry gives the names of the overseers, the child, the master, the date, and the trade to be taught. Virginia bound out orphans AND 'children whose parents could not support them or who failed to educate or instruct them' - SO A LIVING FATHER IS NORMALLY NAMED. TWO CAUTIONS. (a) PRINCE WILLIAM IS DEAD GROUND: its Overseers of the Poor minutes survive only 1788-1802 (Dettingen Parish, published Historic Dumfries 1976) and the county is an LVA Lost Records Locality. FAUQUIER IS THE ONLY CANDIDATE COUNTY WHERE THIS RECORD SURVIVES FOR 1828-36 - and the county where the family demonstrably was in 1823-35 - so the test is cheap and bounded. (b) DO NOT USE LVA's 'Virginia Untold: Indentures of Apprenticeship, 1777-1893': it is free and indexed and it is the WRONG INDEX - Virginia Untold is LVA's African American narrative project and that series covers indentures of free Black and mixed-race children. White apprenticeships stay in the OP minutes and county order books, unindexed. (c) No published abstract covers the target years - the Sparacio/Heritage Books Fauquier Minute Book Abstracts stop in the 1780s; reel 116 must be read directly. PREMISE TO TEST FIRST: OP binding presupposes a destitute or dead father, so the theory needs Thomas poor.
